name: ABORT
behavior: Type-0x10 softkey/state handler at 0x406EC: tests bit 12 of state word $b1e0.w and, if set with $b1fe.w==0x12, JSRs the low-mem A7-API routine $4d8.w to abort the current active-function/measurement state; otherwise returns.

name: ABS
behavior: Shared handler 0x434E6 (also AC): copies calibration/trace RAM blocks out of cal RAM 0x2FC016 into low-RAM working buffer $9EB6 (length validated via fcn.61EC), conditionally copies 0x2FCB42->$A01E when $bfee.w>0x218f, and 0x2FC91A->$A096 — stages cal/trace data into RAM scratch.

name: AC
behavior: Shares the exact handler at 0x434E6 with ABS: block-copies cal RAM 0x2FC016->$9EB6 and 0x2FC91A->$A096 (plus the conditional 0x2FCB42->$A01E), moving calibration/trace RAM regions into low-RAM working buffers.

name: ACP
behavior: Handler 0x3E448: link A6, pushes D0, BSRs fcn.3E3E6 then JSRs low-mem A7-API routine $6802.w before returning — a thin dispatcher (adjacent-channel-power measurement setup) whose real work is in fcn.3E3E6/$6802.

name: ACPCONTM
behavior: Handler 0x702E: thin wrapper that saves D0 and BSRs fcn.6F78 (the ACP continuous-measurement routine) then returns; actual behavior lives in fcn.6F78 which was not disassembled.

name: ACPE
behavior: Handler 0xED78: parses the argument token bytes (checks for the 0x04,0x23('#'),0x41('A') sequence, else dereferences D0), extracts channel count into $b1f8/$b24c, then loops calling ADCXFR (fcn.B3F4) and ADCSHOW (fcn.B9D6) with $ba7c/$ba7e params — runs the extended adjacent-channel-power measurement.

name: ACPGRAPH
behavior: Handler 0x3FBF8: on query (D0==0) reads state via $18a.w and derives a value from the $b0a6/$b0a7 ACP-graph state word (sign-extending the packed byte field), calling fcn.71E4/70D2; on set it merges the argument into $b0a6.w — toggles/sets the ACP graph display mode.

name: ACPSNGLM
behavior: Handler entry 0x4063A: loads mode enum D1=-1 (moveq #-1) and JMPs the shared mode-setter fcn.3E702 — one arm of a jump table that selects the ACP single-measurement mode value and dispatches to the common setter.

name: ACTDEF
behavior: Handler 0x28436: initializes ring/list pointers $b02e,$a996,$a992 to $bffe, then loops over a 12-entry table at 0x2842A computing A7-bus DAC port addresses 0xFFF700+2*idx, writing #$8000 to each port and reading them back into a $a706-area buffer — resets/initializes the 0xFFF700-series analog DAC ports (active-function default).

name: ACTVF
behavior: Handler 0x5ACB2: calls the menu-partition loader fcn.5AA88 and fcn.5A552, builds a 4-entry menu vtable (clears/sets word fields near $9AA6, seeds $8000|masked $ab76), and initializes active-function menu state $956A=0,$956C,$956E,$9544 — sets up the active-function menu/display.

name: ADCPBKT
behavior: Handler 0x184A2: writes #$2FFF to the A7-bus coarse-YTO DAC $f704.w, masks $b212.w, calls low-mem A7 routines $718/$766 and fcn.17546/fcn.5B0DA, then reads the POST self-test latches $f610/$f612 (masking 0xEC) and clears accumulators $b218/$b21c/$b220 — an ADC pass-band/bucket diagnostic sweep.

name: ADCSETUP
behavior: Handler 0xABD0: writes command word #$0002 to the serial interface command port $f5fc.w (0xFFF5FC) and #$8100 to data port $f5fe.w (0xFFF5FE), then returns — configures the SCI/ADC serial interface (a sibling routine at 0xABEC also copies a 4-word default table into cal RAM 0x2FC004).

name: ADCSHOW
behavior: Handler 0xB9D6: from byte coordinates $ba74/$ba75 it computes packed display-region words (ori #$9070 into $ba6c, plus $ba6e/$ba70) defining the on-screen rectangle where the ADC/measurement readout is drawn.

name: ADCXFR
behavior: Handler 0xB3F4: clears SCI command port $f5fc.w, polls ready bit1 of $f5fd.w, then writes #$8000, D0, and the stack-arg word to data port $f5fe.w (0xFFF5FE) storing results to $ba80/$ba82 — performs a serial ADC/DAC value transfer over the SCI.

name: ADD
behavior: Handler 0xD6B2: issues an HD63484/SCI command stream through $f5fc/$f5fd/$f5fe — WPR 0x080C=0x4003, WPR 0x080D=0xFC00, block-write 0x5800 followed by D0,0x3F,0xFF — then polls status bits 5/2 of $f5fd.w; a display-RAM graphics block operation, not arithmetic.

name: ADEFSCL
behavior: Handler 0x317A0: dereferences structure pointer $a89a->A4, compares word fields (A4+0x14) vs (A4+0x16), and if they differ calls fcn.3177C with param 0x3F (returning its result), else returns 0 — a default-scale/range check on the addressed data structure.

name: AMB
behavior: Unresolved (handler_pc=0, not reachable via the dispatch tables); by name and arg-type 0x17 this is the trace-math 'A minus B' operation (store trace A - trace B into trace A), but no disassembly confirms it.

name: AMBPL
behavior: Unresolved (handler_pc=0, not resolved via dispatch tables); by name and arg-type 0xC1 this is the trace-math 'A minus B plus display line' operation (A - B + reference display line -> A), but no disassembly confirms it.

name: AMPCOR
behavior: Amplitude-correction editing entry: gated on the active-function register $b1e4==0x34, it drives function id 0x1f through low-mem slots ($5fe query-active, $42a activate, $616, $610) and reads status registers $b1f8/$b1f9/$b073/$b212/$ad65 to pick the correction-table edit mode.

name: AMPLEN
behavior: Parses a numeric argument (slot $6112, arg count in $b0c8) into 32-bit RAM var $ad5a, then clamps it into one of two ranges ([0xC350..0x53EC60] or [0x1388..0x1E8480]) depending on a mode/units bit0 returned by fcn.223a2.

name: AMSG
behavior: Display/annotation redraw for the active trace: selects a graticule region index from $b070 bit0, pushes width 0x190, calls display slots $544/$5ce, and conditionally slot $562 when $b1e0 bit c is set and $b1e4 is in the range (6,0xB).

name: ANNOT
behavior: Handler did not resolve via the dispatch tables (pc=0); by name and arg type 0x18 this is the screen-annotation on/off control. Best-effort meaning only.

name: ANNOTCTRL
behavior: Parses a numeric argument (slot $7978) into $b0ec and sets redraw flag $b05a=1, then clamps the value into 0x1D..0x29 (special-casing 0x1D or 0x16 based on the $bfee model check) — an annotation position/mode control.

name: ANNOTCTRLA
behavior: Reads the display-list/menu structure pointer at $956a and, if bit 7 of field (-0x61AE,A4) is set, calls subroutine 0x4f31c; the effect of that thin sub-dispatch is unresolved.

name: ANNOTCTRLS
behavior: Stores the argument longword-pair to $b068 and sets $b0a1 bit0 (redraw); clears $ad65 bit3 and, unless $ad65 bit4 is set, activates functions 0x31/0x32 via slot $42a, then drives the display via slot $54a4.

name: APB
behavior: Shares handler 0x28436 with AXB (arg 0xFF). Sets up buffer pointers ($b02e/$a996/$a992 -> $bffe) then loops 12 entries writing 0x8000 to A7-bus analog-DAC ports at 0xFFF700+2*i and reading back 0xFFF702+2*i (comparing vs -5). The disasm is an analog-DAC access, not the expected A+B trace math, and the shared PC with arg 0xFF makes the name mapping doubtful.

name: APNDT
behavior: Handler did not resolve via the dispatch tables (pc=0); by name and arg type 0x02 this is most likely an append operation (trace or display-list append). Best-effort meaning only.

name: AT
behavior: Copies calibration data blocks from cal-RAM (0x2FC016.. length 0x168, transferred via slot $61EC) into low working RAM $9EB6, and gated on the $bfee model check copies further blocks 0x2FCB42->$A01E and 0x2FCA1C->$A198 — loading cal/attenuator correction tables.

name: ATA
behavior: Same handler as AT (0x434e6, arg 0x10): copies cal-RAM correction tables from 0x2FC0xx into working-RAM buffers $9EB6/$A01E/$A198 (the latter two gated on the $bfee model check).

name: ATAN
behavior: Not arctangent: a measurement/state control bracketed by writes of 0x305 (entry) and 0x306 (exit) to sequencing reg $bffe; it manipulates flags $ab76/$ab77/$ab7f, calls sub 0x2bed8 with index 0 then 1 (gated on $a9ae/$a9b0), and sets $b1f8 bit a. The exact subsystem meaning is unresolved.

name: AUDSPLY
behavior: Periodic display-state update: initializes counter $b0a8 from ($b0aa>>12)&3+1, resets $b0ac to 0xC9 (copying $b060->$b176 marker) when it reaches 0x3FF, and gated on $b1e4==0x45 / $b070 bit d / $b213 bit 6 calls redraw sub 0x409a6. Purpose inferred as a display refresh; name-to-function link is uncertain.

name: AUTO
behavior: Queries whether active-function 0 is engaged (slot $5FE with D0=0) and, if so, invokes slot $616 (id 0xD) and executes slot $100 with the saved argument — an auto/coupling dispatch (takes no argument, arg_type 0x00).

name: AVG
behavior: Video-averaging/detector hardware control: read-modify-writes shadow register $ada4 into distinct bit patterns (0xC600 then 0x2000 when arg==1; otherwise 0x4600 or 0x8600 selected by the sign of $adae) and writes the result to MMIO register 0xFFF740.

name: AXB
behavior: Same handler as APB (0x28436, arg 0xFF): loops writing 0x8000 to A7-bus analog-DAC ports 0xFFF700+2*i and reading back 0xFFF702+2*i using a 12-entry byte offset table at 0x2842a. The disasm shows an analog-DAC access, not an 'A exchange B' trace op; shared PC and arg 0xFF make the mapping ambiguous.

name: BADDR
behavior: Entry immediately branches to main body at 0x1FF94 (outside the window); the visible path stores the arg-pair to $b068, then subtracts an arg-derived scaled value from amplitude registers $b1a8 and $b1a6 (tracking sign at frame -0x38). Full behavior unresolved because the main body is out of range.

name: BITF
behavior: Bit-field hardware-port output: gated on $ad4d bit0, writes control word $ad3c to the port pointed to by $ad48 and 0 to the port at $ad44. (The linked entry at 0x256DA additionally writes $ad3a, reads the port back, masks bits 0xC, and toggles $b0e4 bit9 via slots 0x2a/0x2e.)

name: BLANK
behavior: Real handler at 0x30768: reads $9fbc/$9fbe and $b0d0 from RAM, runs fixed-point scaling (jsr $611c/$61ec), then clamps the result to the 0..0xFFF 12-bit range and stores it, and separately compares a value against 0x186a0 (100000). Computes a clamped display/coordinate value rather than obviously erasing anything, so the 'blank' name is not clearly supported by the code.

name: BML
behavior: Shares a table-dispatched handler at 0x28436 (with BTC/BXC/CALFLTDATAX) that seeds scratch pointers $b02e/$a996/$a992=$bffe then loops ~12 entries indexing a byte table at 0x2842a to form A7 analog-bus port addresses 0xFFF700+2n (direct YTO/DAC word ports), writing 0x8000 and reading back into a $bffe buffer, comparing against 0xFFFB(-5). An A7-bus register walk/margin self-test; per-command semantics (arg 0xFF) are not resolvable from this shared code.

name: BRD
behavior: Stub at 0x5ED70: 'move.w #$7d00,D0; rts' — returns the constant 0x7D00 with no side effects.

name: BTC
behavior: Same shared handler as BML at 0x28436: walks A7 analog-bus ports at 0xFFF700+2n (writes 0x8000, reads back into the $bffe scratch buffer, compares to 0xFFFB) using an index table at 0x2842a. Which specific action BTC selects (arg 0xFF) cannot be determined from the shared code.

name: BUFCLR
behavior: Handler at 0x101C6 jumps over an inline byte table (0x101c8), tests $b204.w bit15 (returns 0 if set) else masks $b078.w with 0x7f and indexes the 0x101c8 table, returning the looked-up byte in D0. Behaves as a state/table-lookup query on $b204/$b078, not a buffer clear.

name: BUFSTAT
behavior: Buffer-status query. BENCH-VERIFIED: `BUFSTAT?` -> `0`. Native handler 0x40816.

name: BWR
behavior: handler_pc 0x25FD2 falls inside the ROM boot-menu default-state template (165 words of data, per rom_annotations/MEASURE_MODE_HANDOFF), not executable code — the dispatch table mis-resolved this entry, so disassembly is garbage. By name/kind BWR is a memory/board write, but the actual handler is unverified.

name: BXC
behavior: Same shared A7-bus walker at 0x28436 as BML/BTC: writes 0x8000 to and reads back the direct A7 DAC/register ports 0xFFF700+2n into the $bffe scratch buffer, comparing to 0xFFFB. Per-command (arg 0xFF) meaning is not recoverable from the shared handler.

name: CAL
behavior: Handler at 0x2FFF4 writes analog-control select/data word pairs to the 0xFFF750(select)/0xFFF752(data) register port: select 0x7D60 then data 0x12C, then select 0x5FE0 then a variable data word from the local frame — programming analog/DAC control registers as part of the calibration routine.

name: CALATN
behavior: handler_pc 0x315AA lands in a ROM data/string-table region (frequency-unit and dB-unit suffix strings; real code such as a strcmp begins at 0x315F8), so the dispatch mis-resolved this entry and the disassembly is not the handler. By name a calibrate-attenuator command, but behavior is unverified.

name: CALATNDATA
behavior: Leaf helper at 0x3D4C2 computes a cal-attenuator data block offset/size from the buffer pointers $bb4a.w and $bb4e.w minus 0x780(*2=0xF00) entries, loads index 0x211 (*2) and calls the buffer/address routine jsr $61FE — i.e. it locates the attenuator (flatness) cal-data array (arg_type 0x05, block data).

name: CALFLTDATA
behavior: Handler at 0x40DAA reads $b0aa.w, extracts (>>8)&0xF, divides by 5 and sets D0 = (that == 2) — returns a boolean state query on the $b0aa mode/filter word (related nearby code also checks $b0aa low byte and can emit error 0x4d).

name: CALFLTDATAX
behavior: Routed to the shared A7-bus walker at 0x28436 (with BML/BTC/BXC): writes 0x8000 to and reads back the 0xFFF700+2n A7 DAC/register ports into the $bffe scratch buffer, comparing against 0xFFFB. The specific filter-data-X action (arg 0xFF) is not resolvable from the shared code.

name: CALMXRBIAS
behavior: Handler at 0xC084 copies a 10-word template from ROM (PC-rel $bff4) into a stack param block, computes a span from the $c(A6)-$8(A6) args, then derives a mixer-bias cal-data address as $a914 + (arg<<10) masked to a 16-byte (0xFFFFFFF0) boundary — sets up the mixer-bias calibration data region.

name: CALMXRDATA
behavior: Handler at 0x2E77C calls setup routines ($2bc44/$2ba64), sets $ab7f.w bit7, and gated by $ab77.w mode bits stores the arg byte into a RAM buffer indexed by the $ab82.w / $ab80.w pointers at base offset -0x564e, then clears $ab7f.7 — writes mixer calibration data bytes into the cal buffer.

name: CALTGX
behavior: Handler at 0x20F06 dispatches on the arg (0..10) via a jump-offset table at 0x20F0E (bounds-checked through jsr $862), each case calling $20EA0 with a different flag mask in D0 (0x000, 0x800, 0x100, ...) plus the $8(A6) argument — a tracking-generator calibration subcommand selector.

name: CAMPCOR
behavior: Accessor family at 0xAB76 uses an indexed register port: writes a select byte (e.g. 0x84/0x88, or the arg) to 0xFFF5FC and reads/writes the data word at 0xFFF5FE (returning the high byte, or merging arg<<8 into the low byte on write) — reads/writes the amplitude-correction register(s) via the select/data port pair.

name: CAT
behavior: Handler at 0x30536 normalizes trace length $b0e6.w, sets the display-array pointer $9552.w into $b1d8/A5 (clearing the first word), processes 0x191=401 trace points via jsr $6bb0, honors $b070.w bit8 and $ab77/$ab76 flags, updates via jsr $5d4/$43c/$41e, and checks $b1e4.w (menu register) against 0x70 — redraws/refreshes the trace display array.

name: CATONEV
behavior: Boolean predicate (tag 0x10 softkey/state): returns TRUE (0xFFFF) only if bit 13 of $bc64.w is set AND the classic-command letter register $b1e4.w == 0x34 AND the hardkey-menu register $b1ee.w is 0x60 or 0x61; i.e. it tests whether the catalog display is active on a specific menu. No writes.

name: CATPOS4
behavior: Handler did not resolve via the dispatch tables (pc=0, tag 0x30, arg 0x05); undocumented. From the name and the referencing DLP macro ('CATPOS' in an IF/ELSE block), best-effort meaning is memory-card catalog cursor/position handling (variant 4) — exact behavior unconfirmed.

name: CATREG
behavior: Catalog/save-register select: stores D0, bounds-checks $ab7c.w (<=20) and $a9b0.w (>=0x28), clears bit0 of state byte $ab77.w, clamps the register value via helper 0x2dbea (limits to 0x270f..0xd121), writes the result to $ab8a.w and conditionally into $ab24.w — manipulating the memory-card catalog register RAM block.

name: CENTROID
behavior: Reads scratch/cal-RAM word $2fc00c.l, transforms it via helper 0x1955c and writes it back, then walks the table at ROM 0x19544 to find the index whose entry first meets/exceeds the value, adds the arg offset, clamps to [1, table[0]] and returns the interpolated table value — a marker/graph centroid computation.

name: CHP
behavior: Channel Power measurement: validates the floating-point argument (helpers 0x5af4/0x54bc plus an F-line FP op), then runs a timed measurement loop (0x6882/0x5be8/0x47fc) polling the 0x4824 time-window until bit0 is set — integrating power over the ACPBW channel bandwidth.

name: CHPGRAPH
behavior: Jump-table entry: loads selector D1=3, at 0x40644 pops the return frame and sets A0-A2 (param table at 0x4068a), then tail-jumps to the shared graph/measurement dispatch routine at ROM 0x3e702 which branches on the D1 selector — the channel-power graph member of that command family.

name: CLIPTITLE
behavior: Converts the arg's low nibble to an ASCII digit ('0'+n) and writes it into the title/CLIP text buffer at $acca.w via char-output helper 0x69c8, then calls 0x26282 — building the plotter CLIP title string in RAM.

name: CLRAVG
behavior: Clear-Average: resets the average/sweep counter $b0ac.w to 0x3ff, reads $b0ab.w and calls 0x19fb2, fires redraw/event notifications via 0x42a with codes 0x11/0x12 (and 0x37 if $9e50 set), and clears averaging status bits (mask 0x220e/0x2208) in status word $b1e0.w — resetting the video-averaging accumulator.

name: CLRBOX
behavior: Drives the HD63484 ACRTC (command port 0xFFF5FC, data port 0xFFF5FE, status-poll bit1 of 0xFFF5FD): writes command words 0x0800/0x0801 with the arg as a coordinate, then sends the parameter block at ROM 0xb922 via 0xa91c — draws/clears a rectangular box region on the CRT.

name: CLRDSP
behavior: Clear-Display: resets the display-list pointers $b02e.w/$a996.w/$a992.w all to $bffe, then loops 12 times over the offset table at ROM 0x2842a computing MMIO addresses 0xFFF700+2*offset and writing 0x8000 to each while reading back the paired port — blanking/reinitialising the 0xFFF700-block display registers.

name: CLRW
behavior: Registered handler at 0x223a2 is a predicate returning bit4 of trace-mode word $b213.w (clear-write mode active?) as a boolean; the adjacent helper at 0x223b6 (not the entry) programs the A7 analog bus via select port $f728.w and data port $f72a.w.

name: CLS
behavior: Gated on display-enable bit15 of $b072.w: copies a ~0x4b-word ACRTC command template from ROM 0xd78c onto the stack, patches it with graticule position/scale from $ba64.w/$ba66.w (with a /8 divide), and sends the built display command block via 0xa91c — drawing/clearing a graticule region.

name: CMDERRQ
behavior: Command-Error Query: reads the pending-error flag via syscall 0x5fe with code 0x26; if an error is pending it formats the message with 0x27972, re-reads via 0x616, and outputs the string with the jsr $100 output routine — returning the last command/syntax error.

name: CNF
behavior: Confidence Test: reads the long at $b068.w/$b06c.w; if zero it patches display-status word $b1f8.w (clears mask 0x80, sets 0x180) and calls 0x20442; otherwise indexes a table by $b0c8.w and runs floating-point math (0x5ad2/0x555a plus F-line ops) on the $b060/$b068 values.

name: CNTLA
behavior: Documented as 'Auxiliary Interface Control Line A' (rear-panel aux interface output control line A; arg-type 0x1C). Handler did not resolve via the dispatch tables (pc=0), so the exact register write is unconfirmed.

name: CNTLB
behavior: Documented as 'Auxiliary Interface Control Line B' (rear-panel aux interface output control line B; arg-type 0x1D). Handler unresolved (pc=0); exact register write unconfirmed.

name: CNTLC
behavior: Documented as 'Auxiliary Interface Control Line C' (rear-panel aux interface output control line C; arg-type 0x1E). Handler unresolved (pc=0); exact register write unconfirmed.

name: CNTLD
behavior: Documented as 'Auxiliary Interface Control Line D' (rear-panel aux interface output control line D; arg-type 0x1F). Handler unresolved (pc=0); exact register write unconfirmed.

name: CNTLI
behavior: Sweep-mode/redraw handler: clears/sets sweep-control bits in $ab76/$ab77, dispatches to the continuous-sweep code ($2d2ee CONTS) or single-shot variant ($2d320->$2d2c2) based on $ab7f bit0, then repaints two trace vector-lists via message #$191 through the display vtables at $9556/$955e using the negated offset from $a9ac.

name: COMPRESS
behavior: DLP trace-math op: loads the 64-bit operand pair from $b068 and works it through the float library ($5ad2/$5556/$5568), comparing against a per-record entry in the trace table indexed by $956a (<<3 = 8-byte records) and the operand at $b084. Concrete register/table touches are clear; exact numeric semantics are not fully pinned.

name: CONCAT
behavior: DLP data/trace op: loads operand $b068 via the float lib ($5ad2/$5532/$5556), indexes a table at -0x50ca(A4) by $b0c8 ((x*2+1)<<3), and if the $b068 operand is nonzero emits display message #$190 ($6688). Registers/tables are clear; precise concat semantics not confirmed.

name: CONTS
behavior: Continuous-sweep command: clears the single-sweep flag $ab77 bit4, clears sweep-mode bits in $ab76 (andi #$87ef when bit15 set), issues internal command 0x2c via jsr $42a, optionally re-triggers a sweep ($2d2c2), and sets status/annunciator bit $b1f8 bit10.

name: CORREK
behavior: Correction on/off/type command: masks the correction-flag word $ab76 (andi #$1fff), and depending on the arg (correction type 1..4, gated on $b0e6>0) either dispatches via jsr $2bc or sets $ab76 bit15/bit13 after querying correction-availability helpers $2b8f8/$2b916.

name: CORREKFLT
behavior: Per-channel correction-table operation on the active measurement state $9ea6 (skipped when $9ea6==-1): tests the per-channel enable flag bit6 at (-0x61ae,A4), and applies float-library correction ($5ad2, msg $6688, $79cc/$61ec) keyed on operand $b068 and index $956a. Mechanism is clear; the specific correction type is inferred from the name.

name: CORREKRLV
behavior: Ref-level correction command: if $b116 bit15 is clear and helper $2f498 reports bit1, strobes analog-control MMIO 0xFFF76E with 0x0007 then 0x000F, then clamps the ref-level correction longwords $b0fe and $b102 to the range [1, 0xFFFF].

name: COS
behavior: Writes the real-time-clock: sets RTC control registers 0xEF401D=0x07 and 0xEF401F=0x05, clamps the arg to <=0x17 (23), splits it to BCD tens/units via divs #10, and writes the tens digit to RTC BCD register 0xEF400B (hours field). Despite the name it drives the OKI RTC at 0xEF40xx.

name: COUPLEmD
behavior: Unresolved (handler pc=0, not reachable via the dispatch tables). From the name, an auto-coupling command that couples a measurement parameter to its default/mode-dependent value; behavior not confirmed from disassembly.

name: CSIZE
behavior: Toggles state-flag $b0a1 bit3 (XOR'd with the arg, then bchg), and when the operand $b068 is zero and the longword $b0a2 lies within frequency-like thresholds (0x4E20/0xC3500/0x30D40) it reprograms via short dispatches ($1ea/$178/$5d4) and checks active-command register $b1e4==3. Numeric semantics unresolved.

name: CTA
behavior: Short trace dispatch: tests arg bit0 at (9,A6) and the trace-state count $b0e6 (>=1), then branches to trace routines at $d622 or $d05a. Targets fall in a table-dispatched region not resolved here.

name: CTM
behavior: Bare leaf accessor at the dispatch target: writes command 0x0088 to the HD63484 ACRTC command port 0xFFF5FC and returns (0xFFF5FE>>8), i.e. reads back an ACRTC/CRT register. No link frame (unlike normal command handlers), so this may be a mis-resolved helper rather than the true CTM body.

name: CTMADC
behavior: Per-channel ADC/correction-table operation on active state $9ea6 (skipped when ==-1): reads/writes the per-channel flags at (-0x61ae,A4) (sets bit7, clears bit6), and computes corrections via helpers $5dec/$609c/$4eb72/$5af4 keyed on operand $b068. Mechanism clear; ADC specifics inferred from name.

name: CTY
behavior: Cal/state restore: block-copies calibration/trace tables out of cal-scratch RAM into working RAM — $2FC016->$9eb6 (length-computed via $61ec), and conditionally (gated on $bfee<=0x218f) $2FCB42->$a01e (0x3C words), $2FC91A->$a096 (0x81 words), and $2FCA1C->$a198 (0x81 words).

name: CTYA
behavior: Bare leaf accessor: the dispatch target is 'move.w $94de.w,D0; rts', simply returning the measurement/ADC-cal state word $94de. Surrounding helpers clear/set $94de/$94e0/$94d6/$948a, so this looks like a mis-resolved getter rather than the full CTYA command body.

name: CTYB
behavior: Shares the identical handler with CTY at 0x434e6: block-copies cal/state tables from cal-scratch RAM ($2FC016/$2FCB42/$2FC91A/$2FCA1C) into working RAM ($9eb6/$a01e/$a096/$a198), gated on $bfee<=0x218f.

name: DATASTAT
behavior: Data-status query. BENCH-VERIFIED: `DATASTAT?` -> `2`. Native handler 0x9CE4.

name: DATEMODEVE
behavior: Unresolved (handler pc=0, arg_type 0xFF query/set). From the name, a set/query for the date display-format mode (e.g. MDY vs DMY); behavior not confirmed from disassembly.

name: DDCMD
behavior: Sets bit 9 of the mode/busy flag word $b072.w then calls the subroutine at $1a6e2 to dispatch the DD-context command; the same $b072.9 flag is later cleared by DISPOSE.

name: DDGET
behavior: Reads the long at $b0a2.w and clamps it to hardware limits (ceiling 0x5F5E100 = 100e6; floored/clamped to 0x4E20 = 20000 or 0xC3500 = 800000 depending on the $b0e4.w mask 0x1100 and the $b0ec.w==0x31 model/mode check), returning the limited value.

name: DDMEAS
behavior: Configures the measurement-mode bit fields in $ab76.w / $ab77.w according to the numeric arg in D0 (bit3/bit0 of $ab77 and the 0x2000/0x4004 field of $ab76), sets $ab84.w=$ab7c.w=1, then triggers a measurement via $2ba64.

name: DDREAD
behavior: Sets $b214.w=7, stores the incoming address/length long-pairs into the pointer registers $b068.w (from 8(A6)) and $b060.w (from D0-D1), then calls the block-read routine $5556 and $1ee28 to read data through those pointers.

name: DDRECS
behavior: Entry bra's to $407d0, which extracts the top 2 bits of $b0aa.w (lsr #6) and calls $407ca to return a small mode/record index (1..N); DEMOD uses this return value as an index into a demod-handler pointer table at $40740-0x6aba.

name: DDRST
behavior: Writes the reset/enable flag $ac02.w = 0xFFFF when the arg's bit0 is set, else clears $ac02.w to 0.

name: DDSEND
behavior: Gated on the active-function register $b1e4.w != 0x34, assembles an output message (params 0xAAAA / $ba82-derived offsets / vtable [$9562]+0x4e) via $ea92/$f288 and emits it through $c084, then outputs a trailing char via $316/$be22.

name: DDSTAT
behavior: Reads two status getters $101c6 and $102a4, scales the result (x10, x8, and 0x1F40=8000 minus value) into screen coordinates, calls DDWRT ($c58a) when $ba6b.w bit1 is set, and tests the sweep/mode mask 0x28 of $b07a.w against $b07e.w.

name: DDWRT
behavior: Reads the two getters $101c6 and $102a4 and computes scaled display coordinates (x10, 0x1F40=8000 minus product) using the calibration scale factors $ba56.w/$ba58.w and the display-mode field 0xE000 of $b0a0.w (special path when ==0xA000, divides by 7).

name: DEMOD
behavior: Demodulator control: after $40dc2/$2c2 it tunes using the offset $b0ae.w through the DSP/math routines $64f0/$643e/$5080/$62a0/$651c, then calls DDRECS ($40740) to get a mode index (subq #1, lsl #2) that selects a handler pointer from the table at (-0x6aba,A4).

name: DERASE
behavior: Erases the DLP user-memory object referenced by the handle in $956a.w by calling the memory-manager $5ae5c (and re-storing the returned handle); when $956e.w bit0 is clear it also posts a status message via $39a with params 0xE9/0x1D7/0xFFEA and writes ~$bef6 to $b034.w.

name: DISPOSE
behavior: Entry bra's to $3824c, which frees the allocation handle $a89a.w via $316fa (if $a896.w is nonzero, then clears $a896), clears bit 9 of $b072.w (the DD-active flag set by DDCMD), and disposes each of the $a4e6.w sub-objects by calling $381e8 in a loop.

name: DIV
behavior: DLP arithmetic DIV operator on user variables: looks up the operand variables in DLP variable segment 0x2000 via $57a/$aa8 (name pointers $bb54 / $a02), guarded by the operand-check $3cd6a, performing the division on the referenced DLP variables.

name: DLPINIT
behavior: Menu-state predicate: compares the hardkey-menu register $b1ee.w against the menu-id set {0x1a,0x24,0x25,0x5c,0x5e,0x60,0x61} and returns (in D0) a boolean that is true only when $b1ee is NOT any of those menus (name suggests init but the handler is a menu-context test).

name: DLPINITWR
behavior: DLP init-write loop: after $43670 setup it repeatedly loads the ROM template pointer $499f4 into $4330c, calls $8a4, and advances the $b068.w write-pointer pair comparing via $54ac until done (the fff8/1111 words are branch-displacement decode noise, so exact loop bounds are unresolved).

name: DLPTERM
behavior: Entry bra's to $3646a, a DLP token-stream parser/terminator: reads the token byte at offset 1 of the source pointer (-4,A6), classifies it via $439a and the bitmasks $5fe056 / $48000080, and dispatches to $31f88/$5dc2/$5dec/$31a14 accordingly; clears $b20f.w bit2.

name: DOCATVMEAS
behavior: CATV measurement watchdog: when $9a6 returns true and $b213.w bit0 is clear, compares the elapsed-time counter $bf12 against 0x493E0 (300000) — if exceeded it sets annunciator 0x1B via $42a and marks $b213.0, otherwise (with $9e50.w==0) it clears annunciator 0x1B via $610.

name: DONE
behavior: Reads the battery-backed BCD real-time clock registers $FFEF4017/$FFEF4015/$FFEF4013, combines the nibbles and converts BCD to binary (x10 + units), comparing against 0x57 (87) / 0x63 (99) to derive a date/time field (after the $59998 setup call).

name: DRAWBOX
behavior: Draws a rectangular box on the CRT: saves the graphics cursor ($b08c X-pair, $b090 Y-pair), repeatedly calls the graphics-primitive emitter $4330c with parameter block $499cc (looping up to 0x32 segments while comparing position $b0ac against 0xC9), then restores the cursor from the stack.

name: DRTSETUP
behavior: handler_pc 0x80ac4 lands in a non-code packed-data region of the 0x80000 image (raw bytes 00/11/10/04/25..., not valid M68K and not ASCII), so it cannot be confirmed as a native handler; name suggests some trace/'DRT' setup but the disassembly is meaningless.

name: DRTYMK
behavior: Reads the DLP/trace state-structure pointer from RAM $a7d6, tests bit0 of $956e; if the structure's state field ($16,A4) doesn't match it runs the DLP source at $5be8e via scheduler $cdc, then stamps that field = 0xFFFF (a trace Y-marker refresh/setup).

name: DRTYMKCTRLtH
behavior: Unresolved (handler_pc=0) — did not resolve through the dispatch tables; appears to be a control-suffixed variant of DRTYMK (trace Y-marker), meaning inferred only from the mangled name.

name: DSPBIAS
behavior: Packs hardware-status flag bits from $b1f0/$b1f6/$b1f8/$b1fa/$b1e0 into the display/DAC control words $b084/$b08c/$b098/$b060 (and sets $b0c2 bit31 when $b1e0 bit13 is set) — the documented status/annunciator aggregation routine fcn.11B9A.

name: DSPLY
behavior: Clamps the incoming value to 1..0x190 (400) via $7978 and stores it to display-position register $b0ac, sets bit6 of display flag $b1f9, then triggers a display refresh (jsr $214, $9ab0, $19c).

name: DSPLYA
behavior: Formats a 32-bit value using a field/cursor index ($b234/$b235) into a local buffer at (-$30,A6) and publishes the buffer address to the display-string pointer $b224 (via formatter at $f41c); handles sign by negating and selecting the $b235 vs $b234 field.

name: DSPLYPSD
behavior: Table-dispatch entry that loads format-selector D1=3 plus descriptor table $4068a, pops the arg longword pair, and jumps to the common display/print routine $3e702 to render one formatted parameter.

name: DSPYTF
behavior: Uses the argument (D0>>4, *8) to index two low-memory longword pointer tables at $342 and $32a, runs each low-nibble selection through conversion routine $69b4, and gates output on display flag $b073 bit6 — computes/displays a tuned-filter (YTF) parameter (semantic label inferred; table-indexing behavior is from disasm).

name: DSPYTFI
behavior: Reads a packed word at $41b6 (low 9 bits masked, upper via >>9), searches the ROM breakpoint table at $3fb44 with a cmp/dble loop and applies /4 (divs #4) arithmetic to derive a band/segment index for an internal YTF display computation (YTF label inferred; arithmetic/table-search is from disasm).

name: EDITAMPCOR
behavior: 4-way editor (selector = arg & 3) for the amplitude-correction (AMPCOR) table: indexes the active field via $b234 with lookup table $a5ec, then calls the shared edit dispatcher $1034a (EDITDONE) plus $33eba to format/commit the edited value.

name: EDITDLP
behavior: DLP (downloadable-program) editor command taking a pointer arg: if the second byte of the string is '?' it queries via $6ef8 using DLP edit state $b0aa, otherwise it matches the token against keyword table $40694 (via $39762) and dispatches the corresponding DLP-edit sub-command.

name: EDITDONE
behavior: Shared editor-commit dispatcher keyed on a mode value on the stack (cases 3/4/5): reads/writes the edited value pair via $6736/$6770 and formats it via $7864/$7942/$5f22; called by the other EDIT* handlers to finalize a field.

name: EDITLIML
behavior: 4-way editor (selector = arg & 3) for the lower limit-line table: indexes the active field via $b234 (table $a5ec), fetches the value from the caller's table pointer ($a,A6), and commits through the shared editor $1034a + $33eba, updating the display via $70ca/$7108.

name: EDITNAME
behavior: Name/label editor keyed on menu-item index $956a: tests mode bits $b072 bit15 and $956e bit0, then indexes per-item name structures in RAM (base offsets -0x6604 / -0x65ec off the computed pointer) to edit the selected save-register/trace name.

name: ELSE
behavior: DLP IF/ELSE flow-control token (shares handler 0x406ec with ENDIF): tests the DLP conditional-nesting flag $b1e0 bit12 and $b1fe == 0x12, and branches/skips the enclosed block via $4d8 accordingly.

name: EN
behavior: Type-0x10 state command that validates (checksum call $61ec) and block-copies calibration/state tables out of CalRAM 0x2fc016/0x2fcb42/0x2fc91a/0x2fca1c into working RAM $9eb6/$a01e/$a096/$a198 (word-copy dbra loops).

name: ENDIF
behavior: DLP ENDIF flow-control token sharing handler 0x406ec with ELSE: closes an IF block by testing the conditional-nesting flag $b1e0 bit12 and $b1fe == 0x12 and resuming or skipping execution via $4d8.

name: ENTER
behavior: Handler at 0x4F5A4 masks two argument fields (stack (-2,A6) and (8,A6)) to 0-7, bounds-checks both <=3 (fail branch 0x4F62C), calls helper 0x4E8AE with pointer args, then computes an indexed offset D6=((2*arg+1)<<3) into A4 and dispatches via jsr 0x5AF4.w. A data-entry terminator that validates two 2-bit selectors and vectors through an indexed table.

name: EP
behavior: Handler at 0x406EC tests menu-active bit 12 of $b1e0.w and checks current-menu id $b1fe.w==0x12; only when both hold does it jsr 0x4D8.w. Conditionally invokes the parameter-edit routine when a specific menu context is active.

name: ERASE
behavior: Handler at 0x28436 (shared verbatim with EXP) initializes RAM pointer cells $b02e/$a996/$a992 to $bffe, then loops 12 times over a PC-relative byte table at 0x2842A building 0xFFF700-block addresses (0xFFF700 + 2*table[i]) — the A7 analog-I/O register bank. Sets up a table of analog-port register pointers; note it does NOT touch the display, and ERASE and EXP resolve to the same code.

name: ERR
behavior: Query handler at 0x3122E calls 0x306DA then inspects error-state RAM: bit 10 and bit 13 of $b0d6.w, $b0ec.w==0x2d, and the OR of longs $b068/$b06c, returning an error code in D0 (0x2d, 1, or 0). Reports the current error/status number.

name: EVNTCNT
behavior: Event-counter query. BENCH-VERIFIED: `EVNTCNT?` -> `0`. Native handler 0x401C0.

name: EVNTSTRT
behavior: Handler at 0x17346 clears bit13 of $befa.w, copies $bf3c->$bf3e, then sets the low nibble of sweep-control word $b20c.w to 4 and writes it to the sweep MMIO register 0xFFF300.w before calling 0x640/0x5A4 and testing $a9a0.w. Arms/triggers a sweep (event start) by writing mode 4 to the 0xFFF300 sweep register.

name: EXITCAT
behavior: Handler at 0x42ED2 calls 0x42EA2 then loads D0=8 and jsr 0x702E.w (a display/menu-state routine). Restores the display state on leaving the catalog (selector 8).

name: EXITDLPEDIT
behavior: Handler at 0x5DF48 read-modify-writes the mode word $b0f0.w — clears the 3-bit field (mask 0x1c, via AND 0xFFE3) and inserts (arg<<2 & 0x1c) — then calls redraw routine 0x5DEA8. Sets a display/mode field in $b0f0 and refreshes, exiting the DLP editor.

name: EXP
behavior: Handler at 0x28436 — identical shared code with ERASE: seeds RAM pointer cells $b02e/$a996/$a992 to $bffe and builds a 12-entry table of 0xFFF700-block A7 analog-I/O register addresses (0xFFF700 + 2*table[i]) from the PC-relative table at 0x2842A. Not an exponent math op; it programs the analog-port register-pointer table.

name: EXTOED
behavior: Query handler at 0x11DA8 computes a boolean in D0 by combining state flags: bit13 of $befa.w, whether $bb6c.w != $bb6e.w, whether $bb64.w < 0, and bit9 of $b1e0.w. Returns a composite true/false status derived from those RAM cells.

name: FACTSET
behavior: Handler at 0x3E3E6 fetches an argument array via jsr 0x2F2.w (count at -0xA, pointer at -0x8), computes a reference value via 0x3E276, then loops accumulating sum of squared deviations (D5=elem-ref; D5*=D5; D6+=D5) and divides by count-1 — a variance/standard-deviation computation over the array. The disassembled arithmetic is a statistics primitive and does not match a 'factory preset' name.

name: FDSPLY
behavior: Handler at 0x59EF0 (after a bra past a mis-disassembled jump table) takes a buffer pointer arg in A4, extracts the high nibble of a byte (lsr #4), ORs 0x30 to make an ASCII digit, and stores it into the buffer at (1,A4). Formats numeric bytes into an ASCII display string.

name: FFT
behavior: Entry realigns to 0x331CC (link A6,#-4); it indexes an array pointer arg (8,A6) by (n-1)*2 to read a word offset, extracts a 5-bit field (lsr #8, and 0x1f) into the (0x10,A6) output, and forms a pointer at DLP-record base $a50.w + offset stored to (0xC,A6), then iterates count 3. This is a table/record-decode against the $a50 DLP region; the higher 'FFT' meaning is not confirmed by the code.

name: FFTAUTO
behavior: Handler at 0x3C4C0 loads D0=0, pushes the original arg, and tail-calls shared routine 0x3A374 (the sibling handler at 0x3C4D2 calls the same routine with a menu-string pointer). Dispatches to 0x3A374 with selector 0 — an auto/on-off style setter.

name: FFTCONTS
behavior: Handler at 0x2DD3C calls 0x2DC60 with selector 0, then pushes two word args (8,A6)/(0xA,A6) and calls 0x2DCAE (the sibling at 0x2DD64 is identical but selector 1). Dispatches to the shared 0x2DC60/0x2DCAE pair with mode 0 — the continuous variant.

name: FFTKNL
behavior: Handler at 0x5CC0E does link A6,#-4, stashes A0, and immediately branches to shared routine 0x5DD76 (not in the disassembled window); the fall-through code at 0x5CC18 is a separate DLP-text scan loop reached only by other callers. The actual FFTKNL behavior lives in the unresolved 0x5DD76 routine.

name: FFTMKR
behavior: Handler at 0x3E1D0 fetches an argument array via jsr 0x2F2.w (count at -0xA, pointer at -0x8), and if count>1 pushes count/pointer and calls 0x6C26.w, returning that result+1 (else 0). A query that searches the array (via 0x6C26) and returns a 1-based index/marker position.

name: FFTMM
behavior: Handler at 0x391D0 does link A6, saves D0, and branches to shared routine 0x3926E (outside the window); the fall-through at 0x391F0 is a separate 0x7F-entry table scan (comparing bytes at A4-0x5AB4 against $a4e6.w) belonging to another caller. The FFTMM behavior itself is in the unresolved 0x3926E routine.

name: FFTMS
behavior: Handler at 0x40D86 checks measurement-state var $b1fe (==0x12 -> no-op), then tests FFT flag byte $b0ab and emits marker char 'M' (0x4D) via syscall $184 when clear, or outputs the $b0ab value via syscall $76C otherwise. Reads FFT/marker state; no DAC/ADC touched.

name: FFTOFF
behavior: Handler at 0x4067C loads selector D1=0x0D and tail-jumps to the shared FFT engine routine 0x3E702, which stores the selector at (-0x2E,A6), calls $2F2 and branches on FFT sub-mode; D1=0x0D selects the FFT-disable path. Mechanical dispatch confirmed; the 'off' semantic is name-inferred.

name: FFTSNGLS
behavior: Handler at 0x2BA16 parses its arg via 0x32C22, calls the selector-0x193 routine $7978, then block-copies words into the ACRTC display list pointed to by [$9556]; if $ab76 bit 14 is set it sets bit 10 of status word $b1f8. FFT single-sweep result blit.

name: FLTERRE
behavior: handler_pc did not resolve via the dispatch tables (pc=0); tag 0x40 / arg_type 0x10 marks it a softkey/state-type command. Name suggests a filter or flatness error state query/report, but no disassembly supports this.

name: FLTINIT
behavior: Handler at 0x128D0 reads and clamps parameter $b0e6 (takes abs value, clamps to <=0x28, defaults to 0xFFF1 = -15 when out of range); when positive it pushes selector 0x191 and updates the display list at [$9552] via $6BB0, clears bit 8 of $b212, and masks the arg to its low nibble. Filter-parameter initialization.

name: FMGAIN8
behavior: handler_pc did not resolve via the dispatch tables (pc=0); tag 0x30 / arg_type 0x07. Name suggests an FM-gain calibration setting, but no disassembly is available to confirm.

name: FMSPAN
behavior: Handler at 0x320FE reads a struct via the arg pointer at (0xC,A6) (skips when the long at +0x80 is <=0), derives an index D3 from D0 (clamped >= -10), and computed-jumps (jmp (0xC,PC,D3.w)) into an unrolled word-summation over samples at A2 — accumulates a span-dependent number of points (FM-span data averaging).

name: FORCECNT
behavior: Handler at 0x32062 calls the selector-0x2A routine $6A98 to obtain a count, then loops comparing longwords from args (0xC,A6) vs (0x10,A6), calling subroutine 0x32038 per element — a bounded count/force loop over a value range (frequency-counter forcing).

name: FORMAT
behavior: Handler at 0x5DE94 is a predicate returning SNE of bit 24 of NOT($bf2a) — reports a format/status flag from the $bf2a event longword. The adjacent setter at 0x5DEA8 loads params $b0f0/$b0f2/$b0f4 into MMIO DAC data port $F768 using register-selects 0xC6/0x4F/0x8F/0xCF written to $F76A.

name: FPKEY
behavior: Handler at 0x306C6 is a predicate returning SNE of bit 18 of NOT($bf2a) — reports a front-panel-key event flag from the $bf2a status longword (adjacent variants at 0x306DA/0x306EE test bits 18/19 and OR them).

name: FUNCDEF
behavior: Handler at 0x11DD4 returns bit 0 of CalRAM $2FC013 as a boolean. The actual user-function definition logic is the adjacent routine at 0x11DF4, which clamps the index to 0-9, multiplies by 0x65 and indexes the per-function record table at CalRAM 0x2FC136.

name: GAINDISP
behavior: Handler at 0x5F150 calls predicate $5ECA2; when its bit 0 is set it runs gain processing ($5E88C, then selector-2 $5E84A), and on that bit 0 writes display-enable word $94E0=0xFFFF and calls $5E384 with 0x92, else $5E364 — updates the gain/reference-level display.

name: GAINTWEAK
behavior: Handler at 0x4282E parses two longword args via 0x32C22; when they are equal it computes a log2 shift-count (repeated lsr.w counting shifts) and calls syscall $178 passing the A5 trace pointer — an IF-gain calibration tweak.

name: GATE
behavior: Handler at 0x3F362 tests the arg char at (0xB,A6) for '?' (0x3F) query, otherwise searches a 4-entry char table at 0x3F36A ('A','I','B','M') against state byte $b039 to select a gate mode, emitting mnemonic tokens via $6EF8/$7108. Time-gating mode set/query.

name: GATESEL
behavior: handler_pc 0x800E4 lands inside a data/token table in the 0x80xxx region that disassembles as ASCII HP-IB mnemonic pairs ('O1 M3 MS O2 M4 MT GZ ...'), not executable code, so the true gate-source-select handler is not at this address and cannot be confirmed.

name: GC
behavior: handler_pc 0x801A6 lands in the same 0x80xxx ASCII/token-table region and disassembles as garbage/data rather than a code handler, so its behavior cannot be resolved from the mapped address.

name: GDRVCLPAR
behavior: DLP trampoline at 0x6B93A pushes source id 0x2BE and source ptr 0x6B67C and calls the DLP scheduler $D18; the macro computes the gate-drive clock period __T from gate pulse width __GGTPWID (__T=1/__GGTPWID, switching to 10/__GGTPWID when __T<=5E6) inside a REPEAT loop — gate-drive clock parameter.

name: GDRVSWAP
behavior: DLP trampoline at 0x6B1EC pushes source id 0x177 and source ptr 0x6B074 and calls scheduler $D18; the macro sets __K=__G-5 and __L=__G+5, bounds-checks both to the trace-point range [1,400], then plots — positions/swaps gate-drive markers +-5 points around __G.

name: GDg
behavior: Handler did not resolve (pc=0); the mixed-case name plus slot 4098 (duplicated with GLh) marks this as a spurious/garbled parser-name-table extraction artifact rather than a real command. tag=0x30, arg=0x09.

name: GETPLOT
behavior: Native handler (tag 0x10): copies the plot/output argument token from the arg string into a stack buffer at (-$2c,A6), tests for empty/'?' (0x3f), calls a token lookup (jsr $6090), range-checks the result to 0..0x31, then pushes 0xffff and dispatches into $17a64 to drive the HP-GL plotter output.

name: GETPRNT
behavior: handler_pc=0x0809cc lands in the 0x08xxxx pointer/data-table region (bytes decode as $0008xxxx longwords, not executable code), so the native disassembly is not valid and behavior cannot be confirmed; by name/tag (0x20) it configures/queries printer output.

name: GETT
behavior: Handler did not resolve (pc=0). tag=0x30, arg=0x00; name suggests a 'get trace/time' query but no code or DLP source backs it, so meaning is a best-effort guess.

name: GLh
behavior: Handler did not resolve (pc=0); mixed-case name and slot 4098 (shared with GDg) indicate a garbled/duplicate parser-name-table entry, not a genuine command. tag=0x30, arg=0x09.

name: GPkP
behavior: Handler did not resolve (pc=0); mixed-case name and out-of-range slot 8194 mark it as a spurious parser-name-table extraction artifact. tag=0x30, arg=0x00.

name: GRAT
behavior: Handler unresolved via the dispatch tables (pc=0) though the command is documented (tag 0x10, arg 0x19); by name it is the graticule on/off display control, but this cannot be confirmed from disassembly.

name: GRC
behavior: handler_pc=0x08029e falls inside the 0x08xxxx pointer-table region (contents are $00080b00.. longwords back-referencing the same segment, not code), so the 'native' disassembly is garbage and the behavior is unverifiable. tag=0x30, undocumented.

name: GRDLYNRM
behavior: handler_pc=0x08075e resolves into the 0x08xxxx non-code data/pointer region, so no valid handler disassembly exists; the name suggests a group-delay-normalize operation but it cannot be confirmed. tag=0x30, undocumented.

name: GSTAT
behavior: General-status query; also the DLP status function GSTAT(n). BENCH-VERIFIED: `GSTAT?` -> `1`. Native handler 0x19522 (dispatches on D0 status index).

name: HAVE
behavior: Native state-capture handler: compares queue pointers $bb96/$bb98, clears $b216, copies the 8-byte state block at $b03e into the $bb82 save buffer, and stores the active-function context registers $b1e4→$bb8a, $b1fe→$bb8c, $b1b8→$bb8e (then conditionally post-processes via $165a8/$12b10 on $b1e1/$b1e0 flags).

name: HN
behavior: Native handler (real code at 0xa5f6): masks the arg to arg&3 and uses it to index a small offset table at 0xa5ec, reading the status byte $b234.w and dispatching to one of several number/HP-IB output routines ($1034a, $70d2, $7068, $708a) to format/emit that value.

name: HNLOCK
behavior: Native handler: clears bits 3-5 of $bc64.w (andi #$ffc7), sets up a softkey/menu context via jsr $6bb0 with A0=$bc2c and index 0x1c, then stores menu pointer $be02→$bc3c and 0xf4→$bc3a — installing the harmonic-number-lock menu/state.

name: HNUNLK
behavior: Native handler: copies DLP include-stack pointer $a90c→$a90a and calls $32298 with A0=$bb54 and $bf66 pushed, manipulating the DLP interpreter's saved include/context stack to undo the lock state.

name: HP
behavior: Native handler: pushes the current DLP record ((A4) from $a68), the name-table base $a02, and the arg word, then calls $32b70 and tail-jumps through the return address — a DLP dispatch wrapper invoking a name-table routine with the current record context.

name: ICOMCMD
behavior: Native handler: parses the arg (pea (8,A6); bsr $31bfc) into a D0-D1 pair, range-checks the arg against 0xf, and conditionally emits one of two command constants (loaded from $37b36 / $37b3e) via jsr $5414 — sending a command word to an internal-communication/IF path.

name: ICOMFRQ
behavior: Native handler: sets bit0 of flag $b20f (saving prior $b224), stores the arg pointer into $b224, reads the active-function class $b1e4 and formats a value (jsr $316, $7a8), then divides $b1e4 by 6 (divs #6) and compares to 3 — configuring an internal-comm frequency parameter.

name: ID
behavior: handler_pc=0x0807f0 points into the 0x08xxxx pointer-table region (contents are $00080f5c.. longwords, not code), so the disassembly is not a valid handler; by name/tag (0x30, documented) this is the standard instrument identification query, but that cannot be confirmed here.

name: IDLET
behavior: Circular-decrements a 16-bit index at struct-offset +0x14 (pointed to by A0) by the command's word arg: if index>=arg it just subtracts arg, otherwise it subtracts arg and wraps by adding the field length at +0x0e, then stores back to +0x14. Advances/wraps a character position within an ID/label field.

name: IDNUM
behavior: Query returns the numeric model code. BENCH-VERIFIED on a real 8593E: `IDNUM?` -> `8593`. Native handler 0x4C530.

name: IDSET
behavior: Computes (($b0aa.w & 0x0f)/5); on the zero case tests $b071.w bit3, calls the menu/table lookup $60a, indexes a pointer table at (-$6aba,A4), and uses $b0ac (offset by 0x11) via $7978 to select/set an ID/menu state entry. Table-driven state setter.

name: IEKMODE
behavior: Clears bit0 of the command's arg byte (local -1,A6) then writes the 16-bit arg word through the pointer arg into *(-$4,A6)->A4. A generic store-word-through-pointer accessor (sets an internal mode word).

name: IF
behavior: Six-instruction conditional: tests bit12 of the mode-flags word $b1e0.w and whether $b1fe.w == 0x12, and only if both hold calls subroutine $4d8; otherwise returns. A state-gated conditional primitive.

name: IFTKNL
behavior: IF-token lookup: if the token index $b0c8.w is zero it loads default longwords from PC table $20d7e, else uses A4=$b0c8*4 to index tables at (-$5fba/-$5fa6/-$5f92,A4) and runs fixed-point math routines $6736/$62b6/$62f4 to compute an IF (intermediate-frequency) value.

name: INITMXRDATA
behavior: Init mixer data: checks the mode $b1e4.w>>1 == 0x0c, then via the measurement/menu struct at [$9562.w] reads offsets +0x50/+0x4e and calls $316 and the routine at $b3f4 to (re)initialize the mixer-parameter block.

name: INLJTPLT
behavior: After jsr $6ef8 (setup) it repeatedly loads stored longword parameters ($9ebc, $9f5c, $9ec0, $9ec4, ...) and emits each with the fixed 3-call sequence jsr $668a / $2c8 / $70ca (size 0x18), serializing a block of state longwords to an output/plot template.

name: INT
behavior: Reads the A7 analog-bus status (bsr $2267c, tests bit0) and $b212 bit8 to gate execution, then sets $b1e0 bit11, invokes fixed-point op $610c with 0x0a, builds a value into local -$2a,A6, and dispatches through the vector table at $22d90 indexed by $b0ee.w. An integrate/measurement function.

name: INTVLSTRT
behavior: Interval-start dump: after jsr $6ef8 it streams a long sequence of interval/gated-sweep config bytes and words ($9f64, $9fd6/$9fd7, $9f68-$9f6b, $9eda, $9edc, $9ede, ...) each through the emit helper $4d89c, serializing the interval-sweep parameter set.

name: INTVLTIME
behavior: Interval-time setter with a small 4-entry jump-offset table (0x12/0x18/0x1e/0x26 at $21132) dispatched via jsr $862; sets up via $21068 and calls the value routines $210f4/$21030 with masks 0x40/0x20 to configure the time-interval (gate/sweep-time) mode.

name: KB
behavior: Calls the keyboard-routing/select helper $224c0 with 0 (which masks $ad7c.w), then transforms the arg through $22b56 (fixed-point via $22afe/$5842) and $22b8c. Touches the keyboard-input routing register $ad7c but the exact numeric transform is only partially resolved.

name: KBDTOCMD
behavior: Real code starts at 0x331cc (a data prologue precedes it). Decodes a keyboard-table entry (base=arg ptr (8,A6)) into a 5-bit command token (word at index, >>8 & 0x1f, stored to *(0x10,A6)) and a DLP record pointer computed from the record-region base $a50.w plus the entry offset (stored to *(0xc,A6)). Maps a keypress to a DLP command record.

name: KBDTOPRFX
behavior: Copies the two pointer args ((8,A6) and (0xc,A6)+4) through the pointer-store helper $3d32c, routing a keyboard entry's prefix pointer pair. A keyboard-to-prefix routing setter.

name: KBDTOSCRN
behavior: Saves $ad7c->$ada2, sets or clears bit5 of the keyboard-routing register $ad7d and loads the input vector $ad76 from $9f48 or $9f4c per the arg's bit0, calls $224c0($ad7c), and on a bit5 change clears $b212 bit8 and refreshes $b0c8. Routes front-panel/keyboard entry to the screen.

name: KBDTOTITLE
behavior: Real code from ~0x1a256 (a short data table precedes it): checks the title-buffer state ($bff0 vs 'G'/0x47, $bfee threshold 0x2192), sets flag $afce, copies $b0ec->$b008, clamps the sweep time $b0a2 to 0x61a80, and calls display routines at $17346 (x2) — routes keyboard entry into the title with associated sweep-time/display setup.

name: KC
behavior: handler_pc 0xc470 is SHARED by KC, KD and KE all with sentinel arg_type 0xFF, indicating the dispatch tables did not resolve these to distinct handlers. The code at 0xc470 is a 7-entry param-table copy loop (from $b30e) followed by an unrelated marker/graph routine at 0xc49c, so it is not a reliable KC-specific handler.

name: KD
behavior: Aliased to the same fallback handler_pc 0xc470 as KC and KE (all arg_type 0xFF), so its true handler is unresolved. The 0xc470 code (7-word table copy from $b30e, then marker/graph code at 0xc49c) is not KD-specific and should not be taken as its behavior.

name: KE
behavior: Shares handler 0xc470 with KEYCLR/KLI/KLIF/LIMIBOT (arg_type 0xFF, a sentinel); the routine is a 7-iteration init loop that copies word entries from ROM table $b30e into a RAM state array near $ba96 and clears the companion cells near $baa4. The 5-name-to-1-PC collision plus 0xFF arg means the name-to-handler mapping is a fallback, not a distinct command.

name: KEYCLR
behavior: Same handler as KE (0xc470): the code re-initializes a 7-entry RAM word array (loads from ROM table $b30e near $ba96, clears near $baa4), consistent with a clear/reset of key or limit state, but five command names collapse onto this one PC with sentinel arg 0xFF so the specific attribution is unreliable.

name: KEYCMD
behavior: Writes control word #$c600 to output cell $ada4, checks readiness via $20dd6, then reads five key-definition bytes from $9f64 and $9f68-$9f6b and emits each through helper $20ea0 with field codes ($300/$0/$800/$100/$200) — it assembles and transmits a multi-field key command packet.

name: KEYDEF
behavior: Clears longwords $9ffa/$9ffe, fetches the arg, then based on model/mode cell $bfee (vs #$2190) selects one of two ROM tables ($42e1a or $42d36) and loads their longwords into key-definition parameters $9f48/$9f4c; for $bff0>0x43 it substitutes the float constant #$4ccccd01 — it programs model-dependent key-definition scaling constants.

name: KEYENH
behavior: Handler_pc 0x3afb6 pushes constant 0 and calls $3adac, which selects key-label buffer $a360 (arg 0) or $a370, validates a per-key flag at (-$5ca2,A4), and parses/copies the argument string (via length routine $7978) into the buffer+2 — it stores an enhanced key label/definition string.

name: KEYEXC
behavior: Fetches the arg, sets flag byte $9544=0xFF, calls $5aa1c with the arg, stores the menu/key id into DLP user-menu register $956a, then indexes descriptor tables at (-$6604,A4) and (-$65ec,A4) using arg*3-derived offsets — it selects/executes a user-defined softkey/menu entry.

name: KEYLBL
behavior: Reads menu/key coordinates $ba7c/$ba7e, calls the table-search routine $37e8e (KL) to get an index, and if found indexes the label-pointer table via $a5e0 and the label-byte table via $a5e8 to extract the key's label substring (testing for byte 0x63 'c') — it retrieves a key's on-screen label text.

name: KEYNUM
behavior: Handler_pc 0x21b80 disassembles to a data table, not code — a monotonically increasing byte sequence with stride 6 (0x0c,0x12,0x18,...), i.e. a 6-byte-stride index/offset table. The dispatch did not resolve to executable code, so the behavior is unresolved.

name: KFACT
behavior: For arg>0 computes (arg-1), divides by 6, and uses the remainder*2 to index ROM table $10152, passing the value to $5b00 and then (arg-1)/6-1 to $687a — an engineering-unit/scale-factor selector that divides the index by 6 to pick a units table entry.

name: KH
behavior: Handler_pc 0x0b606 disassembles to ROM constant data (runs of dc.w $fffc, $000a, etc.), not executable code — the dispatch landed in a data table, so no handler behavior can be attributed.

name: KL
behavior: Linear-searches the word table pointed to by $a5dc for an entry equal to the arg, incrementing the index until a match or until it reaches the count in $a5d8, and returns the index in D0 (0xffff if not found) — a key/label lookup-by-value helper (also called by KEYLBL).

name: KLI
behavior: Same shared handler 0xc470 as KE/KEYCLR (arg_type 0xFF sentinel): re-initializes the 7-entry RAM word array from ROM table $b30e (near $ba96, clearing $baa4). Five names collide on this one PC, so the specific KLI attribution is a fallback and not verified.

name: KLIF
behavior: Same shared handler 0xc470 as KE/KEYCLR/KLI (arg_type 0xFF sentinel): the routine is the 7-entry RAM state-array init (ROM table $b30e -> ~$ba96, clears ~$baa4). The many-to-one PC mapping makes the KLIF-specific behavior unverified.

name: KRUNCH
behavior: Drives the HD63484 ACRTC display controller directly through the command port 0xFFF5FC and data port 0xFFF5FE: writes register selects $82/$88 and reads back pointer bytes, tests flag $ba87.0, then writes drawing parameters (#$e8 with #$8900 data, then $98) — a display-controller register read/program sequence.

name: LBU
behavior: After validating the arg via $306c6, builds a control word from (arg<<12) masked with $880/$3c80, ORs it into the hardware-control shadow $b0ea, and writes $b0ea to MMIO port 0xFFF754 with strobe #$fffe to 0xFFF756; for arg==3 it also clears bit7 of $b0eb — it sets band/attenuator-style analog control bits.

name: LIMDK
behavior: Unresolved (handler_pc=0): the dispatch tables did not yield a handler. Name and the LIM* family suggest a limit-line command (plausibly limit-line delete/key) with arg_type 0x0E, but nothing in the disassembly confirms it.

name: LIMIBEEP
behavior: Handler 0x3cd6a is a predicate that returns true when the arg falls within one of four value bands (1-0x0f9c, 0x1f9f-0x270c, 0x36af-0x464a, 0x55ed-0x6588) via Sge/Sle tests; the caller at 0x3cdb6 uses that result to emit a #$2000 tone through $57a — an in-range check gating a limit-line beep.

name: LIMIBOT
behavior: Same shared handler 0xc470 as the KE/KEYCLR/KLI/KLIF group (arg_type 0xFF sentinel): the 7-entry RAM state-array init from ROM table $b30e (~$ba96, clears ~$baa4). The five-name-to-one-PC collision makes the LIMIBOT-specific behavior a fallback and unverified.

name: LIMIDEL
behavior: Native limit-line-editor handler: calls status routine $346de and, if bit0 set (editor active), writes a 3-word ASCII label ($4b45/$5945/$5843) into buffer $a964.w then dispatches jsr $6688 with the argument word from (-2,A6) — deletes/updates the current limit segment and refreshes its softkey label.

name: LIMIDISPlR
behavior: Unresolved (handler_pc=0, not reached via the dispatch tables); by name a limit-line DISPLAY on/off toggle for the limit-line trace, but no handler disassembly confirms it.

name: LIMIEDIT
behavior: Native handler, same $c470 shared routine as LIMIDONE — copies 7 init words from ROM $b30e into RAM $BA96 and zeroes $BAA4 (limit-editor menu/state init); the per-command distinction is not encoded at this PC.

name: LIMIFAIL
behavior: Native handler at $c056: selects a limit-fail test config by the argument — if D0==0 copies 8 bytes from ROM $bfec into RAM $bad8, if D0==1 copies 8 bytes from ROM $bfe4 into $bad8 (installs one of two limit-test-mode parameter blocks).

name: LIMIFTsS

behavior: Native handler at $348b4: calls segment-add routine $34644 (increments limit-segment counter $a634.w, max 0x28) and, on success (D0 bit0), copies a 10-byte high-limit parameter block (2 longs + 1 word) from a PC-relative ROM constant into RAM $a62a.w — appends/sets the upper limit-line segment.

name: LIMILINE
behavior: Trampoline running a DLP macro that ABS-normalizes value __H into a [1,1000) mantissa while tracking exponent __E in a FOR loop (__E bounded -18..12) — engineering-notation scaling used to format/enter a limit-line value.

name: LIMILO
behavior: Native handler at $321be: derives an index D6=((D0>>8)+D0)&0x1f from the argument, indexes the word table pointed to by low-mem pointer $a32.w, and computes the difference between entry[idx] and entry[idx+1] — a parameterized table lookup selecting the lower limit-line segment value.

name: LIMIMIRROR

name: LIMINEXT
behavior: Native handler, same $c470 shared routine — copies 7 init words from ROM $b30e into RAM $BA96 and zeroes $BAA4 (limit-editor menu/state init); this shared PC does not encode a distinct 'next segment' action.

name: LIMIPURGE

name: LIMISDEL
behavior: Native handler, same $c470 shared routine — copies 7 init words from ROM $b30e into RAM $BA96 and zeroes $BAA4 (limit-editor state init); the specific 'segment delete' action is not distinguishable at this shared address.

name: LIMLI
behavior: Unresolved (handler_pc=0): did not resolve through the master/secondary dispatch tables and is not in the documented 859x command set. Name prefix suggests the limit-line editing family (cf. LIMILINE); arg_type 0x0E, handler not recovered.

behavior: Unresolved (handler_pc=0): no handler found via dispatch, not documented. Name suggests a limit-line 'upper' variant (LIMU*, arg_type 0x0E); best-effort only, behavior unverified.

behavior: Reads a string argument at (-4,A6), string-matches it against ROM table $41d5c via jsr $6a52, then ORs limit/graph state words $b0aa/$b0b0/$b0b6/$b0bc (and tests $b0a8); when set and $bef8 bit10 is on it sets redraw-request bit1 of $a5d5 and issues display subcommand 0x4c via jsr $184.

behavior: Trampoline that installs ONCMD command hooks (DLP): ST->__GTUNCS and GD/GL/GATE->__GTPRGT, so those commands re-trigger the graticule/gate redraw routines (log-graticule setup).

behavior: Dispatch stub: loads selector D1=-1 (moveq #-1,D1) and jumps to the shared block-access routine $3e702, which fetches the argument array via jsr $2f2 and branches on the selector. The specific -1 (read) branch is not traced here.

name: MDS
behavior: Unresolved (handler_pc=0): not resolvable via the dispatch tables and not present in the documented command set (arg_type 0x1A). Best-effort meaning unknown; behavior unverified.

behavior: Trampoline DLP trace-math macro: computes N=K-J+1, copies trace A segment TRA[__J,__K] into scratch TRD, finds the peak index via PKPOS, and computes amplitude __Y=9000-TRD[peak] (mean/threshold measurement over a marker-bounded trace region).

name: MEASOFF
behavior: Native handler at 0x3ec9a: if arg count>1 it fetches an array descriptor (ptr in (-8,A6), count in (-a,A6)) via jsr $2f2, and — guarded by a $aea bit-test — stores the 0xFFFF blank sentinel into element index (count+1) before finalizing with jsr $9ee, blanking a measurement/trace array entry.

behavior: Native handler links, then stores the command argument (D0) into RAM word $9b22 (0xFF9B22) and returns — a one-line setter for a memory/mode selector variable.

name: MENU
behavior: Unresolved (pc=0, arg 0x12): did not resolve through the dispatch tables; by name it selects/activates a softkey menu by ID. Cannot confirm from disassembly.

behavior: Native; parses a secondary keyword byte (accepts 'H'=0x48 or 'N'=0x4e, else raises syntax error via 0x184), then resolves a trace designator through 0x40740, indexes the trace-pointer table (RAM base -0x6aba), sets up display op 0x8300 and reads sweep length $b0ac to merge trace arrays.

behavior: Trampoline running the adjacent-channel-power (ACP) measurement macro chain: __ACPSUD, __M3, __ACPSUM, __ACPICALC, __ACPANTIC, __ACPANLBL, __ACPERR plus a KEYCMD — computes and annotates ACP results (name suggests min-hold but the DLP source is the ACP sequence).

behavior: Unresolved (pc=0, arg 0x11): not resolvable via the dispatch tables; by name a marker-A / marker-amplitude accessor. Cannot confirm from disassembly.

behavior: Native; copies stored state blocks out of cal-scratch RAM (~0x168 bytes from 0x2FC016 to $9eb6, plus 0x3c words from 0x2FCB42 to $a01e and 0x81-word blocks from 0x2FCA1C/0x2FC91A into $a096/$a198) — restores the active instrument/trace state from the 0x2FCxxx CalRAM buffer.

behavior: Trampoline running the display/window re-init macro: EM; ANNOT0 (annotation off); DISPOSE8049 (dispose window 8049); WININIT; ANNOT1 (annotation on); then registers ONCMD ANNOT and ONCMD WINZOOM handlers.

name: MKF
behavior: Unresolved (pc=0, arg 0x15): not resolvable via the dispatch tables; by name a marker-frequency set/query. Cannot confirm from disassembly.

name: MKFCR

behavior: Trampoline running a short DLP macro '__GTCLPAR;NV' — invokes the __GTCLPAR macro (get/clear marker parameter) then NV; likely a marker-to-minimum action (source is short and its trailing token may be truncated).

By name: make the active/reference marker current (delta reference).

behavior: Native but resolves to the shared slot-3 fallback handler at 0x00C470 (arg=0xFF; generic 7-word ROM->RAM table-copy/clear init loop, not a distinct handler). By the HP 8590 name: Marker -> Reference Level (set ref level to the active marker's amplitude).

name: MKSP

behavior: Native (tag 0x40) but resolves to the shared slot-3 fallback at 0x00C470 (arg=0xFF; the generic softkey-state table-copy init loop, not a distinct handler). By name: Marker -> Stop frequency.

name: MKTRACE
behavior: Native handler at 0x3E160: fetches an operand vector via jsr $2f2 (count in (-$a,A6), ptr in D0), then computes the 64-bit sum-of-squares of its N words (muls.w D3,D3; add.l/addx.l into D4:D5) and returns it in D0/D1 — a power/RMS-style reduction. This does not match the conventional marker-to-trace-select meaning, so the table resolution is suspect.

name: MKTRACK
behavior: Unresolved (handler_pc=0, slot 0xFFFB, arg 0x13). By the HP 8590 name this is Marker Track / signal-track ON/OFF — re-centers the signal at the marker each sweep by adjusting center frequency.

name: MKTYPE
behavior: Native handler at 0x5A126: fetches an operand vector via jsr $2f2 into A4, bounds-checks index args at (8,A6)/(a,A6)/(c,A6) against the count, then interpolates — (c,A6) - vector[(8,A6)-1] left-shifted 16 and divided via jsr $6200 by (a,A6) — a fractional/scaled lookup into the fetched array. This array-interpolation behavior does not match the conventional 'marker type' meaning, so the resolution is suspect.

name: MN
behavior: Unresolved (handler_pc=0, slot 0xFFF4, arg 0x12). Per the repo's KEYBOARD_MAP work (e.g. hardkey macro '...CF;MN25;') MN is the DLP menu-select command MN<n> that switches the softkey menu to menu number n.

name: MNSV
behavior: Native but resolves to the shared slot-3 fallback at 0x00C470 (arg=0xFF; the generic 7-word ROM->RAM table-copy/clear softkey-state init loop shared with the marker commands, not a distinct handler). Undocumented; likely a state save/select command (menu- or min-hold-save) but its true handler is unresolved.

name: MOD
behavior: Native getter at 0x209D4: btst #15,$ADC4.w — if the invalid/overflow bit is set returns D0=-1 (0xFFFF), otherwise returns the 16-bit value at RAM $B0C8.w. Mechanically a conditional accessor of $B0C8; the command's higher-level purpose is not evident from this stub.

name: MODEC
behavior: Unresolved (handler_pc=0, slot 0x1004, arg 0x16); did not resolve through the dispatch tables and has no conventional HP 8590 documentation. Undocumented mode-related command; meaning unknown.

name: MOV
behavior: DLP trampoline (0x69BEE: push src, jsr $d18); resolved macro 'IF(__GTCPLV==0);MOV GDRVVBW,1;ELSE;MOV GDRVVBW,0;ENDIF;' sets the GDRVVBW (video-bandwidth coupling drive) flag to the inverse of the __GTCPLV coupled-VBW state — a complete, self-consistent assignment macro.

name: MPRST
behavior: Loops 7 times copying default words from the ROM table at $b30e into measurement-state RAM around $ba96 and clearing the companion state words around $baa4 (indices computed as idx*2 off signed displacements -$456a/-$455c); a measurement-preset/reset of 7 state entries.

name: MPY
dlp_source: KEYCMD39,%IF(LG);IF(ACTVF(LG));HD;AMSG/LIN Scale can not be used for this meas.
behavior: Runs DLP macro KEYCMD39 with a %IF(LG) guard: if LOG scale is active for the measurement it holds (HD) and posts the message 'LIN Scale can not be used for this meas.' — a measurement key-command guard, not an arithmetic op (name misleading).

name: MRD
behavior: Gated on $b218; sets bit 3 of $b20f as a request flag, then validates the current window params $a62e/$a62c/$a630 against the ROM template at 0x348ac and, if they match, restores $a630 from $a632 and calls 0x34690.

name: MRDB
behavior: Pops an integer count arg via the DLP arg-fetch jsr $2f2; if >0 it sets up via bsr 0x3e160 (using the pointer at (-4,A6)) and emits a formatted numeric result through the output-helper chain jsr $5df0/$64f0/$6016/$5e36/$6060/$6802; returns 0 otherwise.

name: MSBIT
behavior: Loads D1 = 0x0C (a measurement field/bit index) and jumps to the shared handler 0x3e702, which pops a DLP arg via $2f2 and reads/writes measurement-parameter state keyed by D1; the exact effect of field 0x0C is not resolved from this stub.

name: MSFIELD
behavior: Initializes a 0x20 counter and scans a measurement-field/marker list via helpers 26ef4/26a2a/26b5a, reading the pointer $ac78 and accumulating $ac7c into a running total (-$10,A6) while tracking the flags $ac76 and bit 4 of $acc9; a field/band accumulate.

name: MWR
behavior: When gated-trace-control (__GGTRCTL==1) it computes the gated time marker (__GTTTMKR) and moves the marker frequency MKF into the DLP variable GDRVGTIM, then re-defines that variable (UDEFPV).

name: MWRB
behavior: Adjacent-channel-power macro: runs __ACPSUD setup, blanks the trace (TRC-8000), does VIEW TRC and marker M1, then invokes __ACPCG to compute/graph the ACP result.

name: MXM
behavior: Annotation/marker cleanup macro: disposes the one-shot handler (DISPOSE ONEOS), restores the ANNOT on-command, clears __AMRFLG, sets PCTAMR to -100, and clears the display (CLRDSP).

name: MXMH
behavior: Thin wrapper that pushes a mode flag of 1 and the command's 16-bit word arg (8,A6) and calls the shared routine bsr 0xeedc (a value/percentage handler), returning via the jmp (A0) tail-return trick.

name: NBWDAC
behavior: Gated-trace window macro (name misleading, not a DAC write): under __GGTRCTL==1, if window vars __V==__Y it swaps windows (__GTWINSWAP), then moves the gate scale __GTGSCL into the DLP variable GDRVSWP and re-defines it.

name: NITS
behavior: Copies calibration/state tables out of the 0x2FC000 scratch cal-RAM into low working RAM: block $2fc016→$9eb6, and (guarded by a build-rev check on $bfee) $2fcb42→$a01e (60 words), $2fc91a→$a096 and $2fca1c→$a198 (129 words each); a cal-table state restore.

name: NNSTLV
dlp_source: VRD ACPPWRTX;VRD ACPMAX;VRD ACPLOWER;VRD ACPUPPER;VRD ACPMKA;VRD ACPERR;VRD CHPW
behavior: ACP results readout macro: issues VRD (variable-read/query) on a series of adjacent-channel-power result variables — ACPPWRTX, ACPMAX, ACPLOWER, ACPUPPER, ACPMKA, ACPERR, CHPW... — to report them over the bus.

name: NPHASE
behavior: Computes a boolean predicate (returns D0=0/1): guarded on $9fb4>1, gets a value via bsr 0x104ba, tests bit 15 of $adc4, indexes a table via $b0c8, compares against $b0ac, and gates the result on bit 13 of $b1e0, bit 10 of $b072 and $b0c2 — a trace/phase-condition flag.

name: OBW
behavior: Occupied-bandwidth config setter: validates the numeric arg (0..0xFFF) then selects a target RAM word by the 2nd char of the parameter string — 'C'→$b1ac, 'F'→$b1aa, 'S'→$b1b0 — and writes the value into it.

name: OFF
behavior: Resolves to the SAME dispatch slot 3 / handler 0xc470 as MPRST (a name collision, arg 0xFF); that code loops 7 times loading defaults from ROM $b30e into state RAM around $ba96 and clearing companions around $baa4, so OFF's true dedicated handler is unresolved.

name: OFSTTWEAK
behavior: Active-window offset macro: reads WINACTIVE? into __WN_VAR_4 and, if it is not the ID-only window (__WN_IDO), moves the video-average VAVG — adjusts the active window's video-average/offset (source truncated).

name: ON
behavior: Menu/softkey enable: gets the arg count via bsr 0x5b16a, matches the arg against the DLP user-menu register $956a, then walks the menu-state table at ~(-$6604,A4) and sets the matching entry's state word to 3 (on).

name: ONCMD
behavior: Native handler: the query form (2nd char '?') emits a token via the output routines (jsr $6ef8/$7108/$708a/$70d2); the command form parses one argument and stores a 2-bit code in bits 14-15 (mask 0xC000) of config word $b0aa.w, arming which trigger the ON-event fires on.

name: ONCYCLE
behavior: Trampoline running a DLP macro that clamps measurement-menu variable __MN[18] to the range 1..4, calls __PKFMB, and conditionally updates FFT/marker state when FFTSTAT is active.

name: ONDELAY
behavior: Trampoline DLP macro that validates the adjacent-channel-power bandwidth against span: resets ACPERR, then increments it when ACPBW exceeds SP or falls below SP/100.

name: ONEOS
behavior: Trampoline end-of-sweep DLP macro that installs __FFTKEYS, disables ANLGPLUS when measurement field MSFIELD(67,15,1) is clear, and forces the sample detector (DET SMP).

name: ONIP
behavior: Trampoline DLP macro that declares and initializes window-manager state variables (__WN_ACT=0, __WN_IDO=-1, __WN_IDA=-1, __WN_VAR_1=0, ...).

name: ONMKR
behavior: Trampoline on-marker DLP macro managing the gate/graph-drive priority variable: copies GDRVPRI into __GGTPRI when __GGTRCTL==1, takes its absolute value, and redefines GDRVPRI.

name: ONMKRU
behavior: Trampoline marker-update DLP macro scaling marker position by the 401-point trace length (__T=401*__GGTPRI) and choosing a plot coordinate (100 or 130) from __Z before plotting (PU).

name: ONMODEX
behavior: Native menu/mode-execute handler: loads the active-window struct pointer at $a7d6, sets bit 13 of $bc64.w, and dispatches on the hardkey register $b1e4 (==0x34) and mode index $b056.w through the $bb54 vtable (fcn.58f42).

name: ONPWRUP
behavior: Trampoline on-power-up DLP macro that sets ACP menu variable __ACPMN=215 and invokes ACP single-measure mode (ACPSNGLM).

name: ONSRQ
behavior: Trampoline on-SRQ DLP macro: when __SOENBL is set, it runs __AMRUN if PCTAM is true, otherwise re-initializes the DLP (DLPINIT/DLPTERM).

name: ONSWP
behavior: Native sweep-state handler: copies sweep-mode byte $b05d->$b05c, snapshots sweep counter $bbbc.w, then jump-table dispatches sweep subroutines (fcn.544b0/fcn.543d8) that update $bbbc/$bbba and clear bit 5 of sweep-flag word $befd.w.

name: ONTIME
behavior: Trampoline on-timer DLP macro that sets gate menu variable __GGTMN=245, holds (HD), and runs the gate-window-tracking routine __GTWINTRK.

name: OP
behavior: Trampoline TOI (third-order-intercept) init DLP macro: DLPINIT with __TOITERM, sets __TOIRFLG=1, refreshes MENU 50, runs __SOONRUN, and arms an ONCMD annotation command.

name: OR
behavior: Native handler shared with PAN at 0x434e6; the code is a state/recall routine that copies saved cal-state blocks from cal-RAM (0x2fc016/0x2fcb42/0x2fc91a/0x2fca1c/0x2fcb1e/0x2fc010/0x2fc037) into working RAM ($9eb6/$a01e/$a096/$a198/$a29a) and status words $b1fa/$b1f6/$b1e0 — the OR-specific meaning is not distinguishable from the shared block-copy code.

name: OUTDAC
dlp_source: IF(MN==202); MENU 0; HD; ENDIF; IF(__WN_ACT); HD; ZMKCP -1,__WN_IDA; MOV __A,ZMK
behavior: Trampoline whose DLP source is window-manager marker handling, not DAC output: clears MENU when MN==202 and, when __WN_ACT is set, copies the active marker (ZMKCP -1,__WN_IDA) and reads its value into __A — the OUTDAC name is misleading.

name: OUTPUT
behavior: Native handler that reads a status/config word from the $b060.w-based table at [$b060 + reg_arg*2], extracts a bitfield defined by two arguments (start bit and width via a 0xFFFF>> mask and shifts), and returns the extracted field through the output routine (jsr $77e).

name: PAN
behavior: Native handler with the same PC as OR (0x434e6) — the shared cal/state-recall routine that restores saved blocks from cal-RAM 0x2fc0xx into working RAM and status words $b1fa/$b1f6/$b1e0; arg_type 0x10 (vs OR's 0x11) selects the variant, but PAN-specific behavior is not visible in the shared code.

name: PARSTAT
behavior: Native parser-status query (PARSTAT?): copies the trailing command-name string into a local buffer, space-terminates it, looks it up via fcn.95e against the $bb54 parser vtable, and on success outputs a status string (ROM constant $3d144) through fcn.6ef8/7154.

name: PAVGGRAPH
behavior: Trace-averaging-graph reference helper (DLP trampoline, src @0x6e422): when the graph-control variable __GGTRCTL==1 it copies the drive reference GDRVREFE into __GGTRE, applies ABS, and redefines the processed-value variable GDRVREFE via UDEFPV — maintains the reference used by the power/averaging graph.

name: PDA
behavior: Native handler at 0x3b3fe: reads window/measure-mode state $b0e6.w (>0) and $b0ec.w (==0x31 test) and dispatches with a selector (1/2/6) either through the low-mem vector jsr $2bc.w or helper bsr $3b27e. The actual action is behind the unresolved $2bc.w table.

name: PDF
behavior: Engineering/SI number formatter (DLP trampoline, src @0x71294): normalizes value __T with exponent __E in steps of 3, DSPLYs the mantissa, then appends the SI prefix char (p/n/'.'=micro/m/?) and the 'S' seconds unit — formats a time value for on-screen display.

name: PEAKS
behavior: Short DLP trampoline (src @0x6d2e0): if __V==__Y it calls __GTWINSWAP to swap the active graphics window; a helper step in the peak-search flow (name does not reflect a full peak-list op here).

name: PHASELOCK
